_comment: C-1 CONTRACT-CONFORMANCE PIN — the reviewable record of WHAT WAS CLASSIFIED.
This file is DATA, not a decision. It does not ratify anything and it is not
itself a design contract: it records (i) the exact bytes of the ratified
OPP-12 C-1 converged contract that were read, and (ii) the classification of
EVERY clause in that document into CHECKABLE / CROSS-REPO / PROSE, so that
scripts/check-c1-conformance.sh can make R-20-H7 mechanical instead of a
human re-reading prose at publish time.
WHAT THE MECHANISM IS WORTH (read this before trusting a green): the gate
this registry feeds is a STATIC, LEXICAL check over source text — a TRIPWIRE
AGAINST DRIFT, not a proof of conformance. It catches the changes a future
contributor would realistically make; it is not a soundness argument against
someone deliberately routing around it. The evasion classes it does not and
CANNOT close — dynamically composed SQL, const/macro-indirected identifiers,
ATTACH aliases and views, conversion surfaces outside the named impl,
normalising comparisons — are enumerated under RESIDUAL SCOPE in
scripts/check-c1-conformance.sh's header. That boundary is stated, not
implied, so a reviewer argues with a documented scope.
WHY THE FULL CLAUSE REGISTRY IS COPIED HERE and not just a hash: a reviewer
must be able to SEE what was classified and why. A bare hash is unreviewable
— nobody can tell from 8740f087... whether the Q6(b) negative-space clause is
actually being checked or was quietly demoted to PROSE. Copying the registry
also makes a lazy re-pin visible: updating only `sha256` to silence the gate
still fails, because the gate compares this registry against its own
implemented assertions in BOTH directions.
WHAT THE CATEGORIES MEAN:
CHECKABLE  — a falsifiable mechanical assertion over THIS repo's as-built
code is possible, and scripts/check-c1-conformance.sh
implements it. `evidence` cites where it holds today.
CROSS-REPO — the obligation is on the MEMEX repo (spec persistence,
register(), promotion policy, the AttributeSpec.index carrier,
the forbidden over-build). Not verifiable from here, and
pretending otherwise would be a false assurance.
PROSE      — no falsifiable mechanical assertion exists: rationale, scope
lines, slot/landing notes, status banners.
⚠ THE AMENDMENT THIS PIN EXISTS BECAUSE OF. The contract was AMENDED at
efa8d584 — clause Q6(b) now reads "for registry-admitted GOVERNED entities
only" and carries the TC-11 pin-A cancellation banner. Before that amendment
the clause mandated minting an anonymous surrogate logical_id, which the
ratified TC-11 pin FORBIDS ever implementing and which as-built code does not
implement. A registry derived from the UN-AMENDED text would have been
permanently red and would have held the breaking-pair publish forever. This
pin is keyed to the AMENDED text, and that is exactly why the contract's
bytes are pinned at all.
HOW TO CHANGE THIS FILE: a contract amendment requires RE-DERIVING the clause
registry from the new text — reading the whole document again and
re-classifying every clause — and re-pinning under review, in the SAME change
that carries the new contract. Recomputing the hash alone is a lie, and
re-pinning to silence the gate is the exact failure mode the gate exists to
prevent. Demoting a CHECKABLE clause to PROSE to clear a red is the same
failure wearing a different hat.
REPRODUCE THE PIN FROM GIT:
git rev-parse 23a436dc:dev/design/record-lifecycle-protocol/OPP-12-C1-converged-contract.md
-> 93694a5602ae205de05a801f256676b921dc39cc   (= git_blob_sha1 below)
git show 23a436dc:dev/design/record-lifecycle-protocol/OPP-12-C1-converged-contract.md | sha256sum
sha256_whitespace_normalized is sha256 of re.sub(r'\s+',' ',text).strip(),
used ONLY to tell the reader whether a divergence was formatting-only. It is
never a substitute for the content hash.

clauses.obligation: Status banner: RATIFIED both sides 2026-07-07; ratification schedules nothing and authorizes no build (build != adopt); provenance of the two-shot loop.
Cohesion seam: FathomDB owns structure & mechanism — projection build/drop is an engine verb taking the specs and an EXPLICIT drop list, returning a delta.
evidence: src/rust/crates/fathomdb-engine/src/lib.rs:8198 (pub fn configure_projections(&self, specs: &[ProjectionSpec], drop: &[String]) -> Result<ProjectionDelta, EngineError>)

clauses.obligation: Memex owns semantics & judgment — which attributes exist, what they mean, which roles they take, the promotion gate; the LLM stays Memex-side.
Q1: roles are a SET of ProjectionRole — the engine carries a ProjectionRole vocabulary and ProjectionSpec.roles has set semantics.
Q1: the optional AttributeSpec.index: Set[ProjectionRole] carrier landed INERT in Commission C (memex 95ed450, persisted, byte-identical round-trip); absent => engine py_type inference.
Q3: the engine is the SOLE projection authority — it diffs the supplied specs against ONE durable registry and backfills, reporting the applied delta.
Q3: an incompatible change on an existing `name` surfaces a DESTRUCTIVE DELTA requiring an explicit drop — never silent data loss.
Q3: omission != drop — leaving a live projection out of `specs` does NOT remove it; removal requires naming it in `drop`.
Q3: Memex runs only the pure `derive: EntityTypeSpec -> [ProjectionSpec]` and holds NO projection state.
Q5: the engine ProjectionSpec is a DERIVED cache re-driven IDEMPOTENTLY — re-applying an unchanged spec diffs to a no-op.
Q5: Memex persists the spec (one durable source of truth); drift resolves TO the Memex spec; no two-registry sync; boot runs load_from_store -> derive -> configure_projections.
Q2 end-state: ONE engine-owned EAV attribute store + property-FTS, with the (attr_name, attr_value) composite index the cheap filterable tier reads.
Q2: the engine builds EAV + property-FTS once and PROJECTS via configure_projections — property-level filter and search are live.
Q2: BREAKING, NO DATA MIGRATION (explicit) — existing attributes are not migrated; the EAV/property-FTS migration defines shape only and backfills nothing.
evidence: src/rust/crates/fathomdb-schema/src/lib.rs:847 (step 24 marker: 'NO DATA MIGRATION (HITL 2026-07-21): shape only, no backfill.')
src/rust/crates/fathomdb-schema/src/lib.rs:848-869 (the step's SQL is CREATE-only; no INSERT ... SELECT backfill)

clauses.obligation: Q2: forbidden over-build (Memex) — no PERSISTED standalone attribute node/table; WorldModelEntityAttribute stays a read-materialized facade shape.
Q2 co-land: Memex repoints set_entity_attribute onto the governed engine-EAV verb and retires the nested-dict interim.
Q2: 'property-level projection does not exist until the co-land (recall rides body-FTS + R-B until then — a scope line, not a gap)' — self-labelled a scope line, and overtaken by the co-land itself.
Q4: the cheap tier (filterable, searchable->FTS) builds IMMEDIATELY, in the same transaction as the apply, and is reported as built.
evidence: src/rust/crates/fathomdb-engine/src/lib.rs:8221 (apply_projection_config(&tx, ...) inside one transaction, committed before return)

clauses.obligation: Q4: the expensive searchable->vector tier carries a dense_readiness axis — EXACTLY {ready, embedding}; `pending` is reserved for the orthogonal admission axis and is not a readiness spelling.

Q4 mechanism refinement: the ENGINE NEEDS NO `provisional` CONCEPT — tiering is expressed entirely through Memex's role-declaration timing plus explicit drop, so no provisional notion exists in engine code.
evidence: src/rust/crates/fathomdb-engine/src/lib.rs (zero occurrences of 'provisional' in any .rs file under src/; the only hits repo-wide are natural-language embedding probe corpora, which are test data, not code)

clauses.obligation: Q4 policy: the expensive searchable->vector projection DEFERS to promote() for provisional types. Timing policy is Memex-owned; the engine only builds/drops what is currently declared.
Q4 policy: a REJECTED provisional drops only the cheap projections, so there is no embedding rebuild-churn. Memex decides what to drop.

Q6(a): filterable + searchable co-land alongside rankable — the role vocabulary is exactly {filterable, rankable, searchable}; searchable->FTS / searchable->vector are TIER LABELS on the sub-objects, not roles.
evidence: src/rust/crates/fathomdb-engine/src/lib.rs:3843-3848 (doc: 'EXACTLY three members'; no ProjectionRole::Vector or ::Fts exists)

clauses.obligation: Q6(a): rankable is GRACEFUL-ABSENT, never blocking — declaring it is legal, the engine defers the build with no error and grafts it on the next idempotent configure_projections.

Q6(b) AS AMENDED: the amendment's own factual assertion — 'no EntityTypeSpec or id_prefix exists anywhere under src/'. As-built agrees with the TC-11 pin, not with the un-amended clause. A perfect negative assertion, checked as one.
evidence: src/ (zero occurrences of EntityTypeSpec, id_prefix or idPrefix anywhere in the tree)

clauses.obligation: Q6(b) amendment: h: is a FIRST-CLASS TERMINAL IdSpace variant, so every hit is l: / h: / p: — the typed id space is total over exactly those three.
Q6(b) amendment: hits are NON-NULL by id — no anonymous node is left unaddressed-by-id. SearchHit.id is a total IdSpace, not an Option.
Q6(b) amendment: anonymous and doc-seeded nodes stay h:<content-hash> PERMANENTLY and are unaddressed only by LIFECYCLE VERB (by design) — a typed refusal, not a fabricated surrogate.

Q6(b) AS AMENDED: a surrogate serves ONLY registry-admitted GOVERNED entities (R-20-SUR) — the anonymous leg is CANCELLED, not deferred; registration never mints an id for a pre-existing anonymous row.

Q6(b): the parenthetical status note on the C-2 typed carrier ('additive stable_id base landed, typed swap not started') and the scope line 'C-1 needs only the space/value split, not the typed carrier'. STALE AS WRITTEN and superseded WITHIN THE SAME CLAUSE by the amendment banner ('the C-2 swap shipped ALONE in 0.8.19'); as-built shipped the typed swap in 0.8.19. Classified PROSE because it is a point-in-time status note about a sibling workstream, not an obligation on as-built code — pinning it as CHECKABLE would hold the publish on an already-superseded parenthetical. FLAGGED for the Steward as a documentation defect to fix at the NEXT amendment.

Q6(b): the 'Why this amendment exists' block — rationale, the note that the cancellation was applied to api-surface.md on 2026-07-12 and never propagated here, and the pointers to structural-lifecycle-contract.md §2(ii) (OVERRULED) and 0.8.20-erasure-and-h-end-state-v4.md §5.
Apply atomicity 1: PERSIST-FIRST — register() durably writes the Memex spec (WMEntityTypeSpec) BEFORE any projection work.
Apply atomicity 2: THEN derive -> configure_projections. The derive step is the Memex-side pure function; the engine half (idempotence) is asserted separately at C1-Q5-DERIVED-CACHE-IDEMPOTENT.

Apply atomicity 3: per-projection atomicity — searchable->vector is async with an ATOMIC dense_readiness flip; a torn `ready`-without-vector is FORBIDDEN (the vector row and its terminal commit in ONE transaction).
evidence: src/rust/crates/fathomdb-engine/src/lib.rs:13662 (fn commit_projection_outcomes — one transaction for the vector INSERT and the terminal)

clauses.obligation: Apply atomicity 4: the apply DOES NOT BLOCK ON EMBEDDING — it returns once the cheap projections are applied and the vector work is ENQUEUED, with readiness reading `embedding` until the embeds land.
evidence: src/rust/crates/fathomdb-engine/src/lib.rs:1208 (notify_new_work — the enqueue-side wake; configure_projections notifies and returns rather than waiting on embeds)

clauses.obligation: Apply atomicity 5: CRASH-HEAL — because the registry is durable and the apply is idempotent, a crash at any point self-heals on the next boot re-derive, which diffs actual vs desired and backfills the gap. No cross-step runtime transaction is required.
evidence: src/rust/crates/fathomdb-engine/src/lib.rs:16513 (fn load_projection_registry — the boot read of the durable registry)

clauses.obligation: Apply atomicity: the residual P2·S0 note — the exact SQLite transaction boundary for the same-transaction tier and the worker-enqueue ordering are FathomDB-internal build detail, not a co-design item.
Defaults: the default embedder is the ENGINE'S SHIPPED DEFAULT (CLS-corrected bge-small); Memex's vector:{embedder} is an OPTIONAL override, absent => engine default.
evidence: src/rust/crates/fathomdb-engine/src/lib.rs:3957 (pub embedder: Option<String> — None means the engine's shipped default)

src/rust/crates/fathomdb-schema/src/lib.rs:436 and :867 (body-FTS and property-FTS are created with the SAME 'porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2')

src/rust/crates/fathomdb-engine/src/lib.rs (the engine issues no CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE property_search_index — no per-declaration FTS table is built from a caller-supplied tokenizer)
